question.text: What will be the total retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood in 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the estimated retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood during 2026, according to the [Good Food Institute](https://gfi.org/resource/state-of-the-industry-downloads/)'s 2027 State of the Industry reports.
question.fine_print:
If the Good Food Institute changes their reporting structure, this question will resolve based upon their first official estimate for the year 2026 made during 2027.

If the Good Food Institute does not release a relevant report before 2028 this question will be annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-04-21: GFI's 2026 State of the Industry report (covering 2025) puts global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood at **$6.6B in 2025**, citing Euromonitor. That is up 8% in nominal terms and 4% after inflation, with volume up 3%. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)
- The figure is global (Euromonitor), not US. The US figure is separate: SPINS shows US plant-based meat and seafood retail sales down 10% to about $1.0B in 2025, with units down 11%. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/?p=85119)
- I could not open the GFI PDF (the file was too large to fetch), so the $6.6B comes from GFI-based press coverage and the question's own background.
- Timing: GFI's last two reports came out in April (April 2025 and April 21, 2026). The 2027 report covering 2026 will probably come out around April 2027, possibly after the stated resolution date of 2027-03-31.

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. No 2026 global estimate from Euromonitor or GFI has been published. Only partial 2026 data from individual regions and companies exists (below).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-10: Russia's Logika Moloka bought plant-based drink brands. Analysts say dairy alternatives are doing better than meat substitutes in Eastern Europe. [intellinews](https://www.intellinews.com/plant-based-dairy-finds-a-more-receptive-market-than-meat-alternatives-in-eastern-europe-481394/)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 revenue was $64.5M, down 8.1% year on year, with volume down 10.9%:
  - US retail fell 13.2% to $24.8M.
  - International retail rose 13.3% to $17.9M, its third straight quarter of growth, led by Europe.
  - Q4 guidance is $54-59M.
  [finviz/press release](https://finviz.com/news/416383/beyond-meat-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), [The Poultry Site](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/11/beyond-meats-q3-revenue-falls-8-1)
- 2026-08: Circana and 210 Analytics data show US refrigerated plant-based meat pound sales down 13.5% in August 2026. Refrigerated and frozen products both fell in dollars, units and volume. This is from a secondary summary; I could not parse the PDF myself. [Circana/210 Analytics PDF](https://assets.noviams.com/novi-file-uploads/pbfa/resources-toolkits/August_2026_210Analytics_Circana_meat_alternatives.pdf)
- 2026 (first half): A secondary report says meat and seafood alternatives did well in Germany and France but fell in the UK and Spain. In GFI Europe's Circana data, German plant-based meat value was roughly flat at about €751M with volume down 1.7%, while UK volume fell 9.4%. [GFI Europe](https://gfieurope.org/european-plant-based-sales-data/)
- 2026-04-21: Circana data for six European countries show plant-based food sales up 5.1% in 2025. Plant-based meat's share of plant-based value sales slipped to 4.4% from 4.7% in 2023. [FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/04/21/plant-based-meat-only-4-of-plant-based-market/)

## 4. Base rates

GFI's global plant-based meat and seafood figures, as first reported each year (Euromonitor):
- 2015: $2.2B (per the question background; GFI's 2023 materials say "2014"). [Food Business MEA](https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/?p=2118469)
- 2022: $6.1B, up 8% in dollars and 5% by weight. [GFI](https://gfi.org/blog/2023-outlook-the-state-of-the-plant-based-meat-category/)
- 2023: $6.4B. [esgmena](https://esgmena.com/gfi-2023-state-of-the-industry-report-plant-based-meat-seafood-eggs-and-dairy/)
- 2024: $6.1B, reported as up about 4%. This implies Euromonitor revised 2023 down to roughly $5.9B. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally), [Food Business MEA](https://www.foodbusinessmea.com/?p=2144264)
- 2025: $6.6B, up 8% (4% after inflation). [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)

What this shows:
- The year-over-year growth GFI reports has run between about +1% and +8% in recent years.
- Headline levels have moved between $6.1B and $6.6B since 2022.
- Euromonitor restates past years, so the newly reported level can sit below the previous year's headline even when growth is reported as positive (2023 to 2024 is the example). Exchange rates (the data is in USD) and inflation also move the nominal number.
- Seasonality does not matter here: this is an annual total.

US subset (SPINS):
- 2022: $1.4B, down 1%.
- 2023: $1.2B, down 12%.
- 2024: $1.2B, down 7%.
- 2025: $1.0B, down 10%.

The US makes up about 15% of the global total and is still falling in 2026. Growth comes from Europe (Germany, France), Latin America and Asia.

## 5. Other forecasts

- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The Kalshi markets supplied with the question (US and UK retail sales, silver, and others) are unrelated.
- I found no published Euromonitor or GFI forecast of the 2026 global figure. Commercial "meat substitutes market" reports use different definitions and are not comparable.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Mid-November 2026: Circana and 210 Analytics monthly US data for September and October.
- Early 2027: Beyond Meat Q4 and full-year 2026 results (Q4 guidance is $54-59M). Oatly and other companies also report.
- Early 2027: Euromonitor's annual database update. Its 2026 estimate and any revisions to 2025 drive GFI's number.
- Around April 2027: GFI 2027 State of the Industry reports, the resolution source. If they appear after the 2027-03-31 date, the fine print still counts GFI's first official 2026 estimate made during 2027.
- Watch the USD exchange rate against the euro and Asian currencies: a weaker dollar raises the dollar-denominated global total.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-04 (released about 2026-04-21): GFI's 2026 State of the Industry report on plant-based meat, seafood, eggs, dairy and ingredients puts 2025 global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood at about $6.6 billion. That is up 8% in nominal terms and about 4% after inflation, with purchase volume up about 3%. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/us-alt-meat-slump-continues-but-plant-protein-gains-traction-in-beverages-gfi), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/gfi-state-of-the-industry-report-2025-2026-plant-based-sales/)
- The global figure comes from **Euromonitor** retail data in nominal US dollars. GFI's US figures come from SPINS, and the two are not comparable. I could not open the PDF itself because it is too large to fetch. [vegconomist](https://vegconomist.com/studies-numbers/gfis-2026-state-of-industry-reports-detail-mixed-year-alternative-proteins-across-three-sectors)
- Timing: last year's report came out in mid to late April 2026. That is after the question's stated resolve date of 2027-03-31, so the 2027 report may also arrive in about April 2027.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. GFI has published no 2026 estimate, and the Euromonitor full-year 2026 data will not exist until early 2027.
- Euromonitor's figures are reported in nominal USD, so the 2026 value depends on exchange rates as well as real demand. Most of the category's sales are outside the US. I did not check how the dollar moved in 2026.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-10: Logika Moloka in Russia bought plant-based drink brands. Analysts say dairy alternatives are doing better than meat substitutes in Eastern Europe. [intellinews](https://www.intellinews.com/plant-based-dairy-finds-a-more-receptive-market-than-meat-alternatives-in-eastern-europe-481394/)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 revenue fell 8.1% to $64.5M:
  - US retail fell 13.2%, with volume down 20.8%.
  - International retail rose 13.3%, its third straight quarter of growth, led by Europe.
  - Q4 guidance is $54-59M. [finviz/press release](https://finviz.com/news/416383/beyond-meat-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), [ThePoultrySite](https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/11/beyond-meats-q3-revenue-falls-8-1)
- 2026-08 (Circana data):
  - US refrigerated plant-based meat dollar sales were about $22.7M for the month, down 10.2% year on year, with pounds down 13.5%.
  - Frozen meat alternatives fell 7.8% to $61.4M.
  - Refrigerated items carried per store were down 10.4%. [Circana/210 Analytics](https://assets.noviams.com/novi-file-uploads/pbfa/resources-toolkits/August_2026_210Analytics_Circana_meat_alternatives.pdf)
- 2026 (secondary report): Circana data for H1 2026 reportedly shows strong meat and seafood alternative sales in Germany and France versus H1 2025. I could not find the underlying category totals.
  - Planted's steak more than doubled its sales in the first seven months of 2026.
  - HappyVore's April 2026 sales rose 62% year on year. [Green Queen](https://greenqueen.com.hk/planted-foods-vegan-meat-plant-based-steak-sales-germany/), [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/happyvore-vegan-plant-based-meat-france-sales-nestle-garden-gourmet/)
- 2026-06: GFI Europe reported for 2025:
  - French plant-based meat volume rose 16.8% as prices fell.
  - German plant-based meat sales were €751M, the largest plant-based category there. [GFI Europe](https://gfieurope.org/blog/europes-plant-based-food-retail-market-grows-as-prices-become-more-competitive-but-good-taste-remains-key/)
- 2025 (SPINS): US plant-based meat and seafood sales were about $1.0B, down 10% in dollars and 11% in units, after falling 7% to $1.2B in 2024 and 12% in 2023.

## 4. Base rates
GFI global plant-based meat and seafood retail estimates, as first published each year (Euromonitor):

| Year | Value | Change | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | about $5.6B (€5.15B) | n/a | [search summary](https://gfi.org/blog/2023-outlook-the-state-of-the-plant-based-meat-category/) |
| 2022 | $6.1B | +8% dollars, +5% weight | [GFI blog](https://gfi.org/blog/2023-outlook-the-state-of-the-plant-based-meat-category/) |
| 2023 | $6.4B | described as slight growth | [Supermarket Perimeter](https://www.supermarketperimeter.com/articles/12800-report-alternative-proteins-becoming-more-mainstream-around-the-world) |
| 2024 | $6.1B | +4% | [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/?p=79076) |
| 2025 | $6.6B | +8% (about +4% real) | see section 1 |

- The 2024 figure ($6.1B, +4%) is lower than the first-published 2023 figure ($6.4B), even though it was reported as growth. This means Euromonitor revises past years, likely through restatements and changes in exchange rates. Each report's stated growth rate is measured against a revised base.
- First-published values moved by -5% to +8% from one year to the next, with a range of $6.1B to $6.6B over 2022-2025. Stated year-on-year growth has run from about +1% to +8%.
- Applying the historical range of stated growth (+0% to +8%) to $6.6B gives about $6.6B to $7.1B. A revision like 2023 to 2024 could push the number lower. This is arithmetic, not a forecast.
- The broader global plant-based total went from $28.6B (2024) to $28.9B (2025), reported as +3%. That gap also points to base revisions.
- Seasonality does not apply here, because the figure is an annual total.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the Kalshi markets supplied with the question (silver, US/UK retail sales, FX) matches it.
- I found no expert forecast of Euromonitor's 2026 global plant-based meat figure. Generic market research reports, such as those from The Business Research Company, use different definitions and are not relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11 to 2027-01: Circana and SPINS monthly US updates, including year-end 2026 US data in January to February 2027.
- Q4 and full-year 2026 results from Beyond Meat (around late February to March 2027), plus other companies' updates such as Oatly-type peers and Nestlé or Unilever category commentary.
- Early 2027: Euromonitor's full-year 2026 data release.
- Around March to April 2027: GFI's 2027 State of the Industry reports, which settle the question.
- The dollar's 2026 average against the euro, the yuan and Latin American currencies will affect the nominal-USD Euromonitor figure.

Sources: the links given inline above.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The answer will be known when GFI publishes its 2027 State of the Industry report, most likely around April 2027. That is about 5 months away, possibly a little after the stated 2027-03-31 resolution date.

(b) **Latest known value:** Global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood were $6.6 billion in 2025. This is a Euromonitor figure, published in GFI's report of 2026-04-21. It was up 8% in nominal terms and 4% after inflation, with volume up 3%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** $6.6 billion.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** About $6.7 to $6.9 billion, which is +2% to +5% nominal growth.
- The US, about 15% of the total, is still shrinking at roughly 10 to 13% a year. That subtracts about 1.5 to 2 percentage points from global growth.
- International markets are growing: Germany and France are roughly flat to up, Beyond Meat's international retail is up 13%, and Latin America and Asia are growing.
- The dollar weakened in 2025, which helped the 2025 nominal figure. Exchange-rate effects in 2026 are less clear.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Reported year-over-year growth has ranged from about +1% to +8%.
- Headline levels have moved between $6.1 billion and $6.6 billion since 2022.
- Euromonitor revises past years. The 2023 headline was $6.4 billion, yet the 2024 headline was $6.1 billion even though growth was reported as positive. Revisions of around ±5% are therefore possible, on top of real growth.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** There are no prediction markets or published forecasts that match this definition. Company data points to a weak US market and moderate growth elsewhere. A rough consensus would put nominal growth in the low single digits.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Euromonitor revises 2025 down sharply, as happened with 2023, and the US decline spreads to the UK and Spain while the dollar strengthens. That could produce about $5.5 to $5.9 billion. GFI could also change the reported category definition, pushing the figure lower still.
- **High:** The dollar weakens a lot, Euromonitor revises its historical figures upward, and Asian and Latin American categories grow strongly. That could push the figure to $7.5 billion or more.

(a) **Time left:** The forecast window closes on 2026-12-31. The outcome will most likely be known when GFI publishes its 2027 State of the Industry report, probably around April 2027, about 5 months from now.

(b) **Latest value:** GFI's report of 2026-04-21 (Euromonitor data) puts global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood at $6.6 billion for 2025. That was up 8% in nominal terms and 4% after inflation.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about $6.6 billion.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- Global nominal growth has run at roughly 4-8% per year. That points to about $6.8-7.0 billion.
- Some 2026 signals are softer:
  - US sales keep falling, about 10-13%.
  - Beyond Meat's global revenue is down, though its international sales are up.
  - Germany is flat and the UK and Spain are declining.
- Allowing for that softness, a central estimate of about $6.7 billion is reasonable.

(e) **Historical variation:** Headline levels from one report to the next have moved between -5% and +8%: $6.1B, then $6.4B, then $6.1B, then $6.6B. Euromonitor restates past years, and exchange-rate moves add noise. A one-year standard deviation of roughly 5-7% is reasonable.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market and no published Euromonitor forecast. Industry commentary points to continued US weakness, offset by modest growth in Europe, Latin America and Asia.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Euromonitor revises its methodology or past figures downward, the US decline accelerates and the dollar strengthens. Together these could produce a figure near $5.5 billion. A change in GFI's scope could also lower the number.
- **High:** The dollar weakens sharply, Asia and Latin America grow strongly, or Euromonitor broadens its category definition. Any of these could push the figure to about $7.8-8 billion.
